SMTO-RST-0014 — An unfinished action was cancelled when SMTO was updated

GUID: e96f380f-444c-4fc1-bfa9-285a46517eb9
Slug: upgraded-operation-requires-review
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • An action that was waiting to finish was cancelled when SMTO was updated. SMTO can't tell whether it partly happened, so it won't redo it automatically.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task that was running before the update and read its last messages to see which action was waiting. That tells you which action you need to check.
  2. Check the file, message or system that action was meant to change, without changing anything yet. The update may have stopped the action after it had already made some changes.
  3. If the action did not happen, start a new task in the conversation asking SMTO to do only that remaining work. The old waiting action can't be resumed after the update, so a new task is the safe way to finish it.
  4. Keep the old task and conversation instead of deleting them. They are the record of what was in progress before the update.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed what the old action did, and a new task finishes only the work that was still missing.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the old task or the data folder.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A retained diagnostic reports a pending operation that was invalidated by a runtime upgrade; no current code path emits it (compatibility template only).

What this means

  • This compatibility template describes invalidated pending work after an upgrade, but no current direct emitting producer is present in the reviewed source. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • This compatibility template describes invalidated pending work after an upgrade, but no current direct emitting producer is present in the reviewed source.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the original emitting version and saved pending/receipt state before applying a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Treat as a historical record from an older runtime: keep the old run, its pending record and receipts, inspect the external effects of that operation, then submit any genuinely unfinished work as a new task on the current version. Do not replay the old pending operation.
  • Preserve the old pending record and receipts, inspect current effects, and use a supported compatible task for remaining work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Original work is reconciled and only deliberately unfinished compatible work is submitted.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
